dedupe_keys.name: ge vernova pslf positive sequence load flow power system planning software

description: PSLF (Positive Sequence Load Flow) is commercial power system planning software sold by GE Vernova Consulting Services, which describes it as precision-driven power flow modeling software for energy planners. The product page lists steady-state, dynamic, short circuit, contingency and time series power flow analysis: steady-state load flow for voltage, reactive power, thermal loading and transfer performance; dynamic analysis of disturbance response, stability, frequency and voltage recovery; three-phase and unbalanced fault studies; outage scenarios to find violations and limiting elements; and sequential power flow cases over time. It models transmission systems of up to 150,000 buses and reads PSS/E .raw, .dyr and .idv files. Coverage: generic software for transmission planning. Format and access: desktop software sold in packages with add-ons for geomagnetic disturbance (GMD) analysis, optimal power flow, node-breaker modelling and Ztools, plus training courses; quotes on request. Licence: proprietary; terms and prices were not read. Caveats: the product sheets (PDF) were not opened; supported operating systems and scripting interfaces were not read. Simulation uses: transmission planning, contingency and dynamic stability studies of the grid, including the effect of generator or line outages. Related records: DIgSILENT PowerFactory (platform-digsilent-powerfactory) is a comparable commercial power system analysis package.
